correctness.rationale: The stated all-length series and leading coefficient are correct. A nonzero matrix is realized exactly when the active support is weakly connected and the degree imbalance is zero or one ordered source/sink pair. Around the oriented triangle the differences are (h,h,h) in the balanced sector, giving (1+z³)/(1−z³) with three independent opposite-arc pair factors and three loop factors. For an ordered endpoint pair, adjoining one sink-to-source arc gives a balanced matrix with that arc count positive; subtracting the forbidden-arc sector and dividing by z gives (z+z²)/[(1−z)³(1−z²)³(1−z³)]. The disconnected balanced supports are multiple loop-only vertices, or a positive two-vertex arc pair plus a positive third loop; a disconnected open sector must have the ordered pair in one component and a positive third loop. These give exactly the stated subtractions. Loop-only one-vertex matrices and the length-one zero matrix are retained. The linear count has leading pole coefficient 7/12 at order seven, hence leading coefficient 7/8640; each code fiber contributes at most one word. The proof's quasipolynomial remark should be read as eventual: the rational function has polynomial part −2, so the quasipolynomial extrapolated to n=1 takes value 3, not the actual value 1. This does not alter the Finding's all-length generating function, asymptotic or code-size assertion.
residual_risks: Finite reachability confirms coefficients, not the all-length formula. The explanatory quasipolynomial remark needs the n≥2 restriction if used as a theorem.
